notes: which==0: create heap "SceExfatfsCommon" (0x7F000, opt {0x1C,1}) -> 0x8101d004; EEXIST if already

name: heap_fini
notes: delete heap

name: pathbuf_alloc
notes: 0x800-byte buffer, reuses up to 4 cached (0x8101d068[4], count @0x8101d078), spinlock @0x8101d000

name: pathbuf_free
notes: returns to the 4-entry cache or frees

name: exfat_malloc
notes: heap alloc under spinlock

name: exfat_free
notes: heap free under spinlock

name: utf8_to_utf16
proto: int utf8_to_utf16(u16 *dst, u32 dstbytes, const u8 *src)
notes: lead bytes 0xC2-0xF4 only (else stop, NUL written); code points >=0x110000 or surrogates are emitted as a 0 unit; >U+FFFF as surrogate pair; stops when dst is full; returns code points converted

name: utf16_to_utf8
proto: int utf16_to_utf16(u8 *dst, int dstlen, const u16 *src)
notes: inverse; invalid surrogate -> stop

name: mnt_reactivate
notes: flags&0x4000: keep only 0x2000 and clear slot[i]->+0x684 for 64 slots (+0xd4); flags&0x2000: m->ops(+0xd0)->mount(+0x28)(m); ok -> flags|=1 (mounted) else |=0x20 (error)

name: pathbuf_free_thunk
notes: tail call pathbuf_free

name: name_parse
notes: validates every component of a UTF-16 path (max 0x105 chars scanned, component <= 0xFF): rejects control chars (except 0x05), '\\' and \"./:<>|*?, empty name -> EINVAL (0x80010016); trailing dots removed; ni+0x41c = 1 while the path consists only of '.'/'..' components (tracked with a depth counter); for the last component decides 8.3 representability: base <=8 and ext <=3 OEM bytes (DBCS chars count 2), at most one dot, no spaces, no a-z, none of [=]+,; -> ni[0]=0 and ni+0x40e = OEM 8.3 name with [=;]+, replaced by '_'; otherwise ni[0]=1 (LFN needed); always ni+8 = copy of the path (0x203 u16), ni+4 = pointer to its last component

name: path_parse
proto: int path_parse(int which, const char *utf8path, name_info **out)
notes: UTF-8 -> UTF-16 (pathbuf), '\\'->'/', drop trailing '/', prefix '/', resolve "." and ".." (above root -> ENOENT), <=0x103 chars (else EINVAL), then name_parse into a new pathbuf

name: u16_strcpy
notes: returns end

name: u16_strncpy
notes: zero pads

name: utf16_to_utf8_n
proto: int utf16_to_utf8_n(u8 *dst, u32 dstlen, const u16 *src)
notes: returns length; -1 overflow, -2 bad surrogate

name: finfo_to_iostat
notes: st_attr=fi->attr(+0x39); st_mode=acl_attr_to_mode(m,attr)|(attr&0x10||attr==0xF ? SCE_S_IFDIR : !(attr&8) ? SCE_S_IFREG : 0); size=fi+8; ctime=fi+0x10, atime=fi+0x1c, mtime=fi+0x28 (6 u16 each, usec 0)

name: path_join_parse
proto: int path_join_parse(int which, const u16 *dir, const char *name, u32 namelen)
notes: dir (UTF-16 -> UTF-8) + '/' + name -> path_parse; returns name_info*

name: fnode_table_lock
notes: fast mutex @0x812b2de4

name: u16_strend
notes: (result unused)

name: fnode_is_orphan
notes: true when the path was cleared (orphaned by delete-while-open) but the fnode still has a drive; otherwise false (the directory branch only evaluates drive_root_cluster and discards it)

name: fh_cluster_cache_init
notes: f+0x280/0x288 = {-2,-2,0,0}; if volume opt bit 0x400 (+0xb0): alloc 0x200-byte cache of 42 {-2,0,0} entries at f+0x27c, count f+0x278=42

name: fh_cluster_cache_reset
notes: same without alloc

name: exfat_shared_init
notes: fast mutex "SceExfatfsSharedResource" @0x812b2de4; heap_init; cp_tables_init if 0x8101d02c; zero UVFAT globals 0x8101d080 (0x295D60) once (0x812b2de0); uvfat_init(&g)

name: attr_to_mode
notes: acl_attr_to_mode | IFDIR(0x1000) if attr&0x10 or 0xF, else IFREG(0x2000) unless volume label (8)

name: drive_mount
proto: int drive_mount(exfat_mnt *m, const char *fs_name, const char *blockdev, void *unused, u32 vflags)
notes: called by vfs_mount with mnt_data->fs_name/blockdev_name and vflags 0x80000001 (device opened read-only) or 0x80000000; opts: vflags bit0 -> 1 (ro), bit1 -> 0x102, else 2 (rw); |0x400 unless assign (m+0xc0) in {sd0,os0,tm0,sa0,pd0} (@0x8101d030); |0x200 for sa0:; uvfat_drive_mount(&g, dev, 1, {m, opts})

name: drive_busy_count
notes: argument is the iofilemgr SceVfsMount (reads mnt->data at +0xC4); finds the drive; returns -1 if the exfat mount was invalidated (flags&0x4000), else the number of fds whose fnode is on the drive plus the number of fnode slots pointing at the drive (fnode table lock held)

name: drive_unmount
notes: for drives not in {sd0 os0 tm0 sa0 pd0}: frees the extent caches of every fnode on the drive and of the drive's root fnode (drive+0x3c8/+0x3cc = root+0x278/+0x27c); then drive_mutex_fini, uvfat_drive_unmount(&g, d, d->opts), d->dev = NULL

name: file_same_entry
notes: same type and same first cluster; a file with size 0 and no cluster matches any other such file of the same type

name: nop
notes: returns r0:r1 unchanged; used as a unique-id/time source stub in lookup/create (fid = its result)

name: drive_cluster_size
notes: drive.sec_per_clus * drive.bytes_per_sec

name: root_open
notes: acl_root_attr (ENOENT -> EINVAL); finds the drive (ENOENT); fnode_get("/") (ENOMEM); path_parse("/"); resets the root fnode's extent cache (allocating it when opts&0x400); first reference: fh_cluster_cache_init; fnode_lookup_child(&g, ni, d, f, NULL) i.e. root init; first reference: fnode_set_dir_chain(root cluster, size); on error releases the fnode

name: vfs_root_fnode
notes: finds the drive by mount (ENOENT if none) and returns fnode_get(&g, drive, "/") (ENOENT on failure)

name: fnode_put
notes: fnode_release(&g, f), errno-mapped (a drive_root_cluster call for directories is evaluated and discarded - no effect)

name: sfn_char_ok
notes: c < 0x7F and one of A-Z a-z 0-9 or $%'-_@~`!(){}^#& (table @0x810153e0); with allow_extra also +,;=[] (table @0x81015408); else false

name: rand_alnum
notes: ksceKernelGetSystemTimeLow() % 36 -> '0'-'9','A'-'Z'

name: name_upcase
proto: int name_upcase(u16 *dst, const u16 *src, int n, uvfat_drive *d)
notes: exFAT drive: each char through exfat_upcase_char(drive upcase table); FAT: ASCII a-z only; stops at NUL or n chars, NUL-terminates; always 0

name: fnode_get
notes: _GetFnode: a live fnode (ref>0, has a name) with the same drive and path gets ref++ and its fds' dirty blocks written back (fnode_flush_fds); otherwise, under the fnode table lock, the first free slot (ref 0) or a new one appended up to fnode_cap (0x1000) is reset (parent -2, first cluster -1 because 0x8101d02c is set) and taken; NULL when the table is full; copies the path and points name after its last '/'

name: uvfat_init
notes: once (0x812b2e24): fd pool 0x7000 bytes = 512 fds (fd_cap), 256 initialised (nfds; index 0 is never handed out); ENOMEM (-0x31) without it; clears the 15 pins; each drive: zeroed, embedded iterator fd bound to its root fnode, root fnode reset and bound to the drive; 1024 fnodes reset (nfnodes), fnode_cap 0x1000

name: drive_mutex_init
notes: fast mutex at d+0x3e0 (attr 0x2002) named "SceExfatfsRoot" + assign name with its first letter uppercased, up to the '0' (ux0: -> SceExfatfsRootUx)

name: drive_lock
notes: -0xF on failure

name: uvfat_drive_mount
proto: int uvfat_drive_mount(uvfat_global *g, const char *dev, int mode, u32 *mnt_opts)
notes: -0x20 no dev; -0x2F if dev already mounted (strncmp drive.dev); -10 no free drive; init drive slot (dev, mode, secbuf=g+0x3ed0+i*0x200, mnt, opts, root fnode); uvfat_volume_mount(g,d); on success drive_mutex_init else clear

name: uvfat_volume_mount
notes: opts&0xFF: 1 ro, 2 rw, else -0x20. No device: ro -> state 2 and 0 (an empty read-only mount), rw -> -8. Returns 0 untouched if any open fd or pin references d, or if it is already mounted (mode != 1 and state != 0). Reads sector 0 into secbuf; no 0xAA55 -> diag_bad_signature, -0x11. Resets the FAT cache: 4 windows zeroed, LRU empty, fat_free not valid, free_hint 2, fatcache_sz 0x800. exFAT (BPB bytes 0xB/0xC zero): BytesPerSectorShift (+0x6C) must be 9..12 (diag_bad_sector_shift) and shift + SectorsPerClusterShift (+0x6D) <= 25 (-0x11); sector > 0x800 -> -0x20. io_size = min(cluster, 512), so always 512. The iterator buffer (io_size+0x200) is allocated (-15). VolumeLength (+0x48) 0 -> -0x22. mnt flags |= 0x1000, fatbits 32, fat_eoc 0xFFFFFFF7, data_start = ClusterHeapOffset (+0x58), root_cluster (+0x60), nclusters = (VolumeLength - ClusterHeapOffset) / spc; the ClusterCount field is not used. Then exfat_find_bitmap + exfat_load_upcase. FAT: BPB_BytsPerSec must be 512 (diag_bad_bps, -0x11), io_size 512; TotSec32 and TotSec16 both 0 -> -0x22. FAT32 when BPB bytes 0x11..0x13 are zero (RootEntCnt and the low byte of TotSec16): flags |= 0x1000, eoc 0x0FFFFFF7, data_start = Rsvd + NumFATs*FATSz32, root = BPB_RootClus. Else data_start = Rsvd + NumFATs*FATSz16, rootdir_secs = ceil(RootEntCnt*32/512). FAT12 vs FAT16 is decided by BS_FilSysType 'FAT12   ' or 'UVFAT12 ' (12 bits, eoc 0xFF7), otherwise FAT16 (flags |= 0x8000, eoc 0xFFF7), not by cluster count. nclusters = (TotSec - data_start - rootdir_secs) / spc, clamped to FATSz*bps*8/fatbits - 2; vol_sectors = TotSec. With opts bit 9 (0x200) on FAT and a FAT of <= 128 KiB, the whole first FAT copy is read into one window (fatcache_sz = FAT bytes, count = nclusters+2), allocation failure -> -15. Success: state 2. Any failure: state 0, the iterator buffer is freed and uvfat_drive_unmount runs

name: diag_bad_signature
notes: empty hook

name: diag_bad_sector_shift
notes: empty hook

name: diag_bad_bps
notes: empty hook

name: exfat_find_bitmap
notes: iterate root dir for entry type 0x81 (Allocation Bitmap) with BitmapFlags&1 == VolumeFlags(@0x6A)&1; d+0xd4=FirstCluster, d+0xd0=index, d+0xd8=DataLength(u64); not found -0x25 -> -0xF

name: exfat_count_free
notes: returns at once if the free count is already valid (fat_free_valid, shared with FAT); finds the bitmap if needed; allocates/flushes the bitmap sector buffer; reads every bitmap sector along the bitmap's FAT chain (ceil(DataLength/bps) sectors), counting clear bits into free_clusters; the padding bits after nclusters in the last byte are discounted; caches the last sector read; fat_free_set(free) marks the count valid; broken bitmap chain -> -0xF

name: exfat_bitmap_flush
notes: writes cached bitmap sector if dirty

name: exfat_bitmap_op
proto: int exfat_bitmap_op(uvfat_global *g, u32 ops, uvfat_drive *d, u32 clus, u32 *is_set)
notes: clus outside 2..nclusters+1 -> -0x20; lowest-free hint raised to at least the root cluster; finds the bitmap if needed; follows the bitmap's own FAT chain to the cluster holding this bit (broken -> -0xF); loads that bitmap sector into the one-sector cache (flushing a dirty one first); ops 1 test -> *is_set (moves the lowest-free hint), 2 clear (free_count_inc), 4 set (free_count_dec), combinable (5 = test then set); remembers the last cluster

name: exfat_load_upcase
notes: root dir entry 0x82: DataLength and FirstCluster; the table is read along its FAT chain and kept in its on-disk (compressed) form in d->upcase (size rounded up to sectors); while reading: entries 0..0x7F must equal ASCII upcase (a-z -> A-Z) else -0xF; every 0xFFFF marker records a run {index of the marker, identity count (next entry)} in a list of 0x800-byte chunks (d->upcase_chunks, tail d->upcase_runs_tail); a rotate-right-and-add checksum over all bytes must equal TableChecksum (+4) else -0xF; no 0x82 entry -> -0xF; failures free everything

name: exfat_free_upcase
notes: frees the up-case table and the run chunk list

name: exfat_upcase_char
notes: index = c, skipping the compressed identity runs (each 0xFFFF,count pair stands for `count` characters); characters inside a run map to themselves; otherwise upcase[index]

name: fnode_seek_cluster
proto: void fnode_seek_cluster(uvfat_fnode *f, u32 clus, int type)
notes: cursor := clus, index 0; clus >= nclusters+2 -> invalid (-2); clus 0 on a FAT12/16 root (type 6, RootEntCnt != 0) -> fixed root size marker; valid cluster -> known cluster count 1; otherwise invalid; first extent slot mirrors the cursor

name: sfn_build_part
proto: u32 sfn_build_part(const u16 *name, u8 *out, u32 n, int *pos, u32 *flags)
notes: 8.3 part (n bytes) from the LFN starting at *pos: spaces skipped (lossy), surrogates -> '_' (lossy), chars failing sfn_char_ok -> a RANDOM [0-9A-Z] char (lossy), a-z upcased (flags|=2); stops at '.'/NUL and pads with spaces; returns chars produced, *pos advanced

name: fnode_extent_add
proto: void fnode_extent_add(uvfat_fnode *f, u32 file_clus_idx, u32 disk_clus, u32 ?, u64 bytes)
notes: extent cache insert: run of `bytes` (rounded up to clusters) starting at file cluster index idx -> disk cluster; the 42 slots are buckets of size (max index/42)+1 that are re-bucketed (merging adjacent runs) when the file outgrows them; tracks the known cluster count (+0x288), the contiguous tail (+0x280 disk, +0x284 index) and the number of discontinuities (+0x28c)

name: exfat_encode_times
notes: finfo -> exFAT File entry: mtime (fi+0x28) -> LastModified (+0xC) with 10ms byte (+0x15) = 100 when the second is odd (DOS 2 s granularity), atime (fi+0x1c) -> LastAccessed (+0x10), ctime (fi+0x10) -> Create (+0x8) with 10ms (+0x14); each is shifted by the entry's existing UtcOffset byte (+0x17/+0x18/+0x16) when set (UTC -> stored local), no offset byte is written; FileAttributes (+4) := finfo attr, DIRECTORY forced for directories

name: fd_load_block
notes: cluster size (FAT12/16 root: fixed root size; clus 0 = root); block index = (pos mod cluster) / io_size; cluster_read_block into fd->buf; fd->buf_block = pos / io_size, buf_clus = clus, +0x34 = block within the cluster

name: fd_share_block
notes: only when the fnode is shared (ref > 1): every other fd of the fnode buffering the same block either receives a copy of this fd's dirty buffer (if it is dirty too) or has its buffer invalidated; then this fd's dirty block is written

name: fd_write_direct
proto: u32 fd_write_direct(uvfat_fd *fd, u32 flags, g, u32 nclus, u32 len, const void *buf)
notes: pos must be io-block aligned (else -0x20); bytes = whole io blocks up to len inside the nclus contiguous clusters (FAT12/16 root: fixed size); unless flags&0x100: invalidates/flushes an overlapping buffered block, fd_share_block, blk_write at cluster_to_sector + offset; mtime := now and dirty (also for allocate-only calls); pos advanced; flags&1: fnode size raised to pos; cluster cursor advanced; returns bytes

name: fnode_next_cluster
notes: fat_access(get); value 0 (free cluster inside a chain) -> notify_broken_chain and -1 (cursor count adjusted); read error -> -2; a valid next cluster continuing the cursor is added to the extent cache; EOC/out of range returned as is, cluster count updated

name: fd_contig_span
proto: int fd_contig_span(uvfat_fd *fd, ?, u64 pos, u64 len, int flags)
notes: (it, ?, u64 pos, u64 len, flags) - used by fd_write and dir_write_raw: how many clusters from it->clus are physically contiguous for [pos, pos+len): flags&1 = file data (bounded by the fnode's size, NoFatChain = sec_flags&2), else the fnode's directory stream as seen from its parent context (parent_size, parent_flags&2); NoFatChain spans are contiguous by definition; otherwise follows fnode_next_cluster while next == cur+1, feeding the extent cache; FAT12/16 root: 1 while inside the fixed area; invalid cluster -> 0

name: fd_contig_read
proto: int fd_contig_read(uvfat_fd *fd, u32 len, u32 clus_bytes)
notes: read-side run length, only caller fd_read: len is clipped to the bytes left before the file size; NoFatChain (sec_flags&2): pure arithmetic, and it moves the fnode's contiguous cursor (cur_clus/cur_idx) forward; FAT: follows fnode_next_cluster while next == cur+1. Returns the number of clusters from fd->clus that the read can cover

name: chain_bytes
notes: walks the chain: clusters x cluster size (FAT12/16 root: fixed size)

name: fd_seek_cluster
proto: int fd_seek_cluster(uvfat_fd *fd, ?, u64 pos, int alt)
notes: target cluster index = pos / cluster size; uses the extent cache (bucket lookup), the contiguous tail cursor, or restarts from the first cluster (alt: the parent-context cluster, i.e. a directory stream); empty file (no cluster) -> -7; FAT12/16 root beyond its fixed size -> -7 (pos clipped); success only when the cursor reaches the target index, else -0x25 (caller walks the chain)

name: fnode_init_root
notes: type 6 (root dir), mode from acl_root_attr, attr +0x249, zero times, first cluster (exFAT/FAT32 root cluster; 0 for FAT12/16), size from chain length

name: fd_seek
proto: int fd_seek(uvfat_fd *fd, ?, u64 pos, u32 flags)
notes: fd_seek_cluster first; on -0x25 walks from the cached point: exFAT NoFatChain (flags&2 selects the parent-context flags for directory streams) resolves arithmetically within the allocated size, FAT follows fnode_next_cluster in contiguous runs, feeding the extent cache; reaching EOC/the end -> -7 with fd->pos clamped to the end of the last cluster; success stores pos

name: drive_root_cluster
notes: exFAT root cluster; FAT32 BPB_RootClus; 0 for FAT12/16

name: fd_seek_alt
notes: fd_seek over the parent-context stream (parent_cluster/parent_size/parent_flags: the directory that contains this fnode's entry), same algorithm as fd_seek; -7 at the end

name: fnode_set_dir_chain
proto: void fnode_set_dir_chain(uvfat_fnode *f, u32 clus, u64 size)
notes: type := 6; fnode_seek_cluster; if the chain is valid: size = given size, or for clus 0 the root size (exFAT/FAT32: walk; FAT12/16: fixed RootEntCnt*32), or the walked chain length; known cluster count := ceil(size/cluster)

name: fnode_set_chain
proto: void fnode_set_chain(uvfat_fnode *f, u32 clus, u64 size)
notes: fnode_seek_cluster(f, clus, f->type); size given -> cluster count from it; size 0: files get an "unknown, unbounded" count, directories get their size from the walked chain (root: as fnode_set_dir_chain)

name: fd_buf_invalidate
notes: buf_block = -1, buf_clus = -2 (0 without CP tables)

name: fat_next
notes: clus 0 = the root's first cluster (exFAT root cluster / FAT32 BPB_RootClus; FAT12/16 root has no chain); valid range: >=2 (exFAT, FAT12/16) or >= BPB_RootClus (FAT32 - clusters below the root cluster are treated as invalid) and < nclusters+2; fat_access(get); invalid or error -> EOC (0xFFFFFFFF exFAT, 0x0FFFFFFF FAT)

name: contig_next
notes: f is a finfo view (fnode+0x210): clus+1 while clus is below first cluster (+0x34) + ceil(size (+8) / cluster), else -1

name: contig_check
proto: u32 contig_check(uvfat_drive *d, u32 first, u32 n, ?, u64 size)
notes: first+n if within size, else -1

name: cluster_find_free
notes: returns a free cluster or EOC. If fat_free <= reserved_clusters and the free count is trusted (fat_free_valid) -> EOC (full). hint outside [2, nclusters+2) -> 0. exFAT: if hint >= free_hint, test the hint's bit (bitmap op 5) and return it when free; else scan the bitmap linearly from max(start, free_hint), where start is the d+bitmap_clus field (last-allocated cursor), wrapping once to free_hint and stopping at the starting point -> EOC. FAT: fat_find_free(d, hint)

name: fd_extend
proto: int fd_extend(uvfat_fd *fd, ?, u64 len, u32 flags, ?, u32 *out)
notes: fd_extend(it, ?, len_lo, len_hi, flags, g, *out_count): grows the cluster chain so it covers it->pos + len. it = {fnode*, ?, u64 pos, ..., +0x18 cur cluster, +0x1c cluster index}. flags bit0 = the fnode's own stream (else the parent-context stream at fnode+0x244..0x26c, i.e. the directory holding the entry), bit1 = directory (fnode_seek_cluster type 6). An empty own stream gets its first cluster from cluster_find_free (exFAT: NoFatChain|AllocPossible flags set; FAT: EOC written). Each further cluster is asked for as prev+1; while the run stays contiguous an exFAT NoFatChain stream stays FAT-less, otherwise the existing run is materialised with fat_set_run(first..last), NoFatChain is cleared and linking continues through the FAT (fat_access set prev->new, new->EOC). Failure frees the just-taken cluster in the bitmap. Errors: -10 (no space; also FAT12/16 fixed root and exFAT dir > 256 MiB), -15 (empty parent stream / bad chain). Updates the parent stream's valid size (+0x268) and resets it->cur cluster/index to the stream start; *out_count = clusters added

name: chain_free
notes: frees a FAT chain from first: for each cluster read the next link (FAT32 clusters below BPB_RootClus treated as end), write 0, and on exFAT clear its bitmap bit (op 2); stops at an invalid, self-referencing or EOC link. Then fat_dirty = 1 and, on exFAT, exfat_bitmap_flush. Does not consult NoFatChain - contiguous exFAT runs are freed with contig_free

name: contig_free
proto: int contig_free(g, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fnode *f, u32 first)
notes: contig_free(g, d, f, first): exFAT NoFatChain span of finfo f (start cluster, size): last = start + ceil(size/cluster) - 1 (> nclusters+2 -> -15); first must lie in [start, last] else -0x20; clears bitmap bits first..last inclusive (op 2), then exfat_bitmap_flush. Size 0 or start 0 -> 0, nothing freed

name: fnode_flush_fds
notes: ref>1: write back dirty blocks of every fd on f

name: fnode_is_entry
notes: true if f names a real directory entry (has drive, path, valid position, not the root)

name: fnode_touch
notes: time_m := now (+0x238), dirty |= 4 (entry needs writeback)

name: dirit_release
notes: drive-private dir iterator: state(+0x11c) 3 -> 0, else -0xF

name: dir_open
proto: int dir_open(uvfat_global *g, u32 fdidx, u32 clus, uvfat_drive *d, u8 flags, int alt)
notes: fdidx != 0: g->fds[fdidx]. Else claims the drive-private iterator d->dirit (mode 0 -> 3, busy -> -15), resets its fnode's cluster cache, type 6, first cluster clus, and sizes it: alt != 0 -> alt bytes; clus 0 -> root size (FAT12/16 RootEntCnt*32, else one cluster to start); otherwise chain_bytes; cluster count = ceil(size/cluster). Then clus 0 on FAT32/exFAT is replaced by the real root cluster, fd_reset, and the iterator fnode's parent context = {d, clus, flags, alt (size)}; buffer invalidated (buf_block -1, buf_clus -2 when 0x8101d02c is set, else 0)

name: fnode_writeback
notes: if f is a real entry (fnode_is_entry rules) and dirty&4: opens the parent directory with dir_open(g, 0, parent_cluster, d, parent_flags, parent_size), positions the iterator at the entry (parent_pos / parent_cluster2, cluster index = pos / cluster; pos -2 or 0 = start). exFAT: exfat_update_entry(g, d, &f->mode). FAT: dir_read_raw the 32-byte entry; empty -> -7; LFN, volume label, deleted (0xE5) or invalid first byte -> -32; else steps back 32 bytes, rewrites ctime (time+date), atime (date only), mtime (time+date), size, first cluster (high word only on FAT32) and attributes (fat_attr_encode) keeping the 10 ms byte, writes with dir_write_raw and fd_flush_block. Releases the iterator (mode 3 -> 0). Root and non-entries -> 0

name: fd_read
proto: int fd_read(g, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fd *fd, void *buf, u32 len, u32 flags)
notes: flags&1 = file (stop at size; else raw stream). Loop: bytes inside the buffered block (buf_block) are copied out. On a miss, a dirty buffer is written back first, and for files that also drive_flushes and stamps mtime + rewrites the entry (fnode_writeback). Then fd_seek (-7 = EOF -> return the count so far). Unaligned, tail or sub-block requests load the block into fd->buf with cluster_read_block (FAT12/16 root: fixed area). Block-aligned requests of at least io_size inside the file go direct to the caller's buffer: fd_contig_read gives the contiguous run, its bytes are trimmed in io_size steps down to len; a dirty buffered block overlapping the run is flushed first; one block -> cluster_read_block, more -> blk_read; then clus/clus_idx advance. Returns bytes read

name: dir_read_raw
notes: returns up to 32 bytes from fd->pos through the fd's one-block buffer, using fd_seek_alt (the stream of the fnode's parent context: parent_cluster/parent_size/parent_flags, i.e. the directory stream set up by dir_open). On a buffer miss a dirty block is written back, then cluster_read_block loads the block (FAT12/16 root: fixed area). Returns bytes copied, 0 at end of stream (-7 from fd_seek_alt), <0 on I/O error. The buf == out shortcut copied from fd_read can never trigger here

name: dir_next_entry
proto: int dir_next_entry(uvfat_global *g, u32 fdidx, u8 *out32, uvfat_drive *d)
notes: fdidx 0: the drive iterator d->dirit (parent_cluster 0 -> real root cluster on FAT32/exFAT); else g->fds[fdidx] (first_cluster 0 -> root cluster). dir_read_raw into out32: 0 ok, -7 at end, <0 error; out32 NULL -> -0x20

name: exfat_dir_find
proto: int exfat_dir_find(int mode, uvfat_global *g, const u16 *name, uvfat_drive *d, finfo *out, u32 fdidx)
notes: mode 0 = lookup by (already upcased) name: name <= 0x100 chars and only on the drive iterator (fdidx != 0 -> -0x20), filter by exfat_name_hash; mode 1 = next entry set (readdir), no hash filter, name copied back into name (<= 0x100). 0x200-byte name buffer (uv_alloc, NULL -> -10). Scans for a 0x85 File entry (type 0 = end -> -7); the next entry must be 0xC0 Stream (a 0x85 restarts the set, anything else skips); mode 0 compares Stream.NameHash. SetChecksum is recomputed over File (bytes 2-3 skipped) + Stream + ceil(NameLength/15) 0xC1 Name entries (15 UTF-16 units each) + the remaining SecondaryCount secondaries, which count only with InUse (bit 7) set, else the checksum is poisoned; SecondaryCount < name entries+1 or a mismatch -> keep scanning. Mode 0 then upcases the assembled name (name_upcase) and u16_strcmp's it, and on a match rewinds the iterator by (SecondaryCount+1)*32 to the set start. out (an fnode): finfo +0x210 zeroed, exfat_attr_decode + exfat_decode_times from File, first cluster (+0x244) = Stream.FirstCluster, size (+0x218) = Stream.DataLength (ValidDataLength is not read), fnode_set_chain; +0x260 = cluster holding the File entry, +0x258 = iterator position, +0x250 = directory cluster, +0x248 = Stream.GeneralSecondaryFlags (NoFatChain). Ghidra's 'unreachable' blocks at 8100f2a4..f2d0 are a 0x85 checksum variant after a confirmed 0xC1, really dead

name: fat_dir_next_sfn
proto: int fat_dir_next_sfn(g, u32 fdidx, uvfat_drive *d, u8 *ent)
notes: next short-name entry: skips 0xE5, LFN (attr 0xF) and volume label (attr&8); an invalid first byte (< 0x21 and != 5) -> notify_corrupt_entry and skip; '.' and '..' (0x2E then ' '/'.' then 9 spaces, constant 0x8101b788) are skipped too; 0 -> -7

name: fat_dir_next_lfn
proto: int fat_dir_next_lfn(g, uvfat_fnode **f, u16 *lfn, ?, u8 *sfn, u32 fdidx)
notes: (g, it, lfn_out, finfo_out, sfn_out, fdidx): reads entries until a short-name entry. LFN (attr 0xF): an ordinal with 0x40 starts a set (count = ord&0x1F, its checksum remembered); following fragments are kept only while their checksum matches - the ordinal sequence itself is not checked; fragment n-1 gets 13 UTF-16 units + NUL. 0xE5 and volume labels drop the pending LFN; invalid first byte -> notify_corrupt_entry. At the SFN the 8.3 checksum must match or the LFN is dropped; '.' / '..' are skipped like fat_dir_next_sfn. Output: lfn = concatenated fragments (<= 0x100, empty if none); sfn = NAME.EXT with every space removed ('.' only when the first extension char is not a space; leading 0x05 -> 0xE5); finfo: fat_attr_decode, ctime (time+date), atime (date), mtime (time+date) - the 10 ms byte ignored -, size = DIR_FileSize, first cluster = lo | hi<<16 (hi only on FAT32); directories (type 6) get size = root size or walked chain length * cluster. 0 ok, -7 end, <0 I/O

name: notify_broken_chain
notes: ksceIoNotifyEvent(mnt_data->mnt_id, 1, {mnt_id, 0x808D0007, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0}) - the cluster argument is not passed on

name: notify_corrupt_entry
notes: same event with code 0x808D0008; the entry itself is not passed on

name: notify_bad_entry_values
notes: posts code 0x808D000B only when the suspicious entry has a first cluster, a non-zero size or the DIRECTORY attribute; the values themselves are not passed on

name: fat_dir_lookup
proto: int fat_dir_lookup(g, uvfat_drive *d, u8 *ent, const u16 *name)
notes: (g, d, ent, name): name is already upcased; empty -> -5; 0x200 name buffer (uv_alloc, NULL -> -10). Scans the drive iterator with dir_read_raw into ent (must be non-NULL - the local fallback is copied but ent is still dereferenced); end / type 0 -> -4. LFN collection as fat_dir_next_lfn (0x40 starts, checksum-matched fragments, no ordinal check); at each SFN entry (0xE5/volume label skipped, bad first byte -> notify_corrupt_entry) the LFN (if its checksum matches) is name_upcase'd and compared, then, if name is < 13 units, the space-stripped 8.3 form (0x05 -> 0xE5) is converted with oem_to_ucs2 and ASCII a-z upcased and compared. Match: the iterator is left just after the SFN entry, ent holds it, and when 0x8101d02c is clear acl_check_read(mnt, attr) < 0 -> -5

name: fd_close_touch
notes: for a real entry (fnode_is_entry rules): drive_flush, time_m := now, dirty |= 4, fnode_writeback; dirty&4 cleared on success; returns the writeback result (0 for root / non-entries)

name: dir_write_raw
proto: int dir_write_raw(g, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fd *dirfd, const u8 *ent32, u32 *grown)
notes: write-side twin of dir_read_raw (it was mis-summarised as a free-slot finder): writes the 32 bytes at ent32 to dirfd->pos in the parent-context stream through the one-block buffer (dirty flag, fd_share_block keeps other fds on the block coherent). An unallocated stream (parent_cluster -1) gets a first cluster from cluster_find_free (exFAT: NoFatChain|AllocPossible; FAT: EOC) - none -> -10. At the end of the stream (fd_seek_alt -7) the directory grows with fd_extend(flags 2), *grown += clusters added; a block in freshly added clusters is zero-filled in the buffer instead of being read (only that block - the rest of the new cluster is left as on disk); block-sized writes use fd_write_direct. Returns bytes written (32) or <0

name: exfat_update_entry
notes: rewrites the exFAT entry set at the drive iterator from finfo fi: File entry (0x85, else -0x20; type 0 / end -> -7) gets exfat_encode_times; the next entry must be Stream 0xC0 (else -0x20): ValidDataLength (+8) AND DataLength (+0x18) both := fi size (+8) - no separate valid length is kept -, FirstCluster (+0x14) := fi+0x34, GeneralSecondaryFlags (+1) := fi+0x38. The remaining SecondaryCount-1 secondaries are read only to recompute SetChecksum (one without InUse, or a 0x85, -> -0x20); the checksum goes to File+2, the iterator rewinds by (SecondaryCount+1)*32 and File + Stream are written back with dir_write_raw, then fd_flush_block

name: fd_write
proto: int fd_write(g, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fd *fd, const void *buf, u32 len, u32 flags, u32 *grown)
notes: flags: &1 file data (fd mode must be 2, 6 or 8 - bitmask 0x22800000 - else -2; size grows with pos), &2 the parent-context (directory) stream, then *grown += clusters added by fd_extend, &0x100 allocate only (buf ignored, nothing copied; used with buf NULL by the chstat/truncate grow path). Loop per io block: a hit in the buffered block copies in, marks dirty and fd_share_block. On a miss a dirty buffer is written back (failing file writes also drive_flush), and for files drive_flush + mtime + fnode_writeback. An empty stream gets a first cluster (cluster_find_free; exFAT NoFatChain|AllocPossible, FAT EOC; none -> -10); at the end of the chain (fd_seek -7) fd_extend grows it for the remaining len. fd_contig_span gives the contiguous run; block-aligned spans >= io_size go through fd_write_direct straight from buf; a partial block is zero-filled in the buffer when it is in a just-allocated cluster or (files) wholly past the old size, else fd_load_block reads it first. With &0x100 a partial block is neither copied nor marked dirty, so allocate-only growth does not zero the tail on disk. Returns bytes written or <0

name: dir_lookup
proto: int dir_lookup(g, const u16 *upname, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fnode *f)
notes: (g, upname, d, f): f carries its directory as parent context (parent_cluster 0 -> real root cluster on FAT32/exFAT; a directory fnode with first cluster 0 gets the root cluster too). exFAT: dir_open(parent_cluster, parent_flags, parent_size) + exfat_dir_find(mode 0) fills f; -7 -> -4. FAT: dir_open + fat_dir_lookup; on a hit parent_pos = iterator pos - 32 (the 8.3 entry itself, not the LFN start), parent_cluster2 = iterator cluster, and the finfo (zeroed 0x40) is filled from the SFN: attributes, ctime/atime/mtime, size = DIR_FileSize, first cluster lo | hi<<16 (FAT32 only); fh_cluster_cache_init + fnode_seek_cluster; size 0 directories get root size or chain_bytes; cluster count = ceil(size/cluster). Both: an entry whose first cluster equals its directory's cluster -> notify_bad_entry_values, still returned as found. Iterator released

name: dir_lookup_name
notes: name_upcase then dir_lookup

name: path_walk
proto: int path_walk(g, name_info *ni, uvfat_drive **d, uvfat_fnode *f, uvfat_fnode *parent_out)
notes: (g, ni, &d, f, parent_out): drive must be mounted (state, dev) else -15; ni+0x41c == 1 -> root (fnode_init_root). Else the UTF-16 path at ni+10 is split on '/', each component name_upcase'd (<= 0x100) and dir_lookup'ed starting from the root cluster; an intermediate that is missing (-4) -> -5, not a directory -> -6. After each intermediate directory, parent_out (if given; exFAT presets its parent_cluster -2) receives a copy of f's finfo and parent context - so it ends up describing the final component's directory - and f's parent context becomes that directory (first cluster, size low 32 bits, sec_flags). The final component's result (0 or -4) is returned with f filled. 0x200 buffer (uv_alloc, NULL -> -10)

name: fnode_lookup_child
proto: int fnode_lookup_child(g, name_info *ni, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fnode *f, uvfat_fnode *parent)
notes: (g, ni, d, f, parent): parent NULL -> fnode_init_root. Else f gets the parent's finfo (mode, type, size, times, first cluster, flags, attr) and parent context = the parent directory (parent_cluster = parent_cluster2 = its first cluster, parent_size = its size, parent_flags = its sec_flags, parent_pos 0); the last component (ni+4) is upcased in place and dir_lookup fills f

name: dir_create_entry
proto: int dir_create_entry(g, const u16 *name, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fnode *f, uvfat_fnode *parent)
notes: writes a new entry for f into the directory parent (its first cluster +0x244, flags +0x248, size +0x218); f->parent_cluster := that cluster. FAT: base and extension come from sfn_build_part (leading dots/spaces skipped and flagged lossy, the extension is taken after the LAST dot, a base > 8 or ext > 3 is lossy, 0xE5 -> 0x05). A name that is exact 8.3 in upper case gets only the SFN, without LFN or a collision scan. Otherwise it gets (len+12)/13 LFN entries, and a lossy name also gets '~1' at min(base length, 6). Collision passes: every live SFN (0xE5, LFN, volume label, '.'/'..' skipped; corrupt ones reported) is formatted NAME.EXT and strncmp'd (SceSysclibForDriver_12CEE649 = strncmp, case-sensitive, 16) against the alias. Each hit bumps the tail number N; its 1-6 decimal digits are placed after a '~' at the first '~' or space, at most 7 - digits; the checksum is recomputed and the scan continues. A pass without hits ends the loop. Free slots: needs that many consecutive 0xE5 entries, or a 0x00 entry, which ends the scan and is then followed by a terminator, or the end of the stream, where dir_write_raw grows the directory. LFN entries are written last-first (0x40 | n), 13 units each, NUL then 0xFFFF padding, the alias checksum at +0xD. The SFN carries ctime (time+date, 10 ms byte 0, NTRes 0), atime date, mtime, attributes (fat_attr_encode), first cluster (hi word FAT32 only; a directory pointing at the root cluster stores 0) and size (0 for directories). Then fd_flush_block and dirty&4 cleared; f->parent_pos/parent_cluster2 = SFN position. exFAT: n = ceil(len/15)+2 entries in a uv_alloc buffer (-10). The search counts entries with InUse clear and stops at 0x00 as above; f->parent_cluster2 tracks the cluster of the run start. File 0x85: SecondaryCount n-1, UTC offset bytes 0x16..0x18 = 0x80, exfat_encode_times. Stream 0xC0: flags = f->sec_flags, NameLength = len as u8, NameHash = exfat_name_hash of the upcased name, ValidDataLength = DataLength = size, FirstCluster. Name 0xC1 entries hold the name as given, not upcased. SetChecksum covers everything. The entries go out with dir_write_raw, counting the clusters added. If the directory grew, the parent's size gains clusters * cluster bytes, its dirty |= 4 and sec_flags = the iterator's parent_flags (NoFatChain may have been dropped), and, unless the parent is the root (parent_cluster -2), its own entry is rewritten (exfat_update_entry) and drive_flush runs. f's parent_size/parent_flags follow

name: dir_delete_entry
proto: int dir_delete_entry(uvfat_global *g, const u16 *name, uvfat_drive *d, uvfat_fnode *f)
notes: deletes f's directory entry by name (callers: remove, rmdir, rename source). The name is copied and upcased in a 0x200 buffer (-10). exFAT: dir_open(parent ctx) + exfat_dir_find(0), -7 -> -4. The File entry is rewritten with type 0x05 (InUse cleared). Then each of its SecondaryCount secondaries is overwritten with that same 32-byte File image retyped 0x40, so stream and name data are destroyed rather than only having InUse cleared. Then fd_flush_block and dirty&4 cleared. FAT: dir_open + fat_dir_lookup; the 8.3 entry gets 0xE5. Walking backwards, every directly preceding LFN entry (attr 0xF) gets 0xE5 until the one with the 0x40 ordinal bit; the LFN checksum is not checked. Then fd_flush_block. Clusters are not freed here; callers do that

name: dir_open_thunk
notes: tail call dir_open

name: fd_rewind
notes: drive iterator or fd: position 0, buffer invalid

name: dir_read_entry
proto: int dir_read_entry(g, u32 fdidx, u8 *out32, u8 *copy32, uvfat_drive *d)
notes: next raw 32-byte entry from the drive iterator (fdidx 0) or g->fds[fdidx] (first cluster 0 -> root cluster); into out32, or copy32 if out32 is NULL; with both, out32 is also copied to copy32. Both NULL -> -0x20, end -> -7

name: blk_flush
notes: if the block device is open (blk_vp, blk_file, blk_fd != -1): vfsLockVnode(blk_vp), ksceVopSync(blk_vp, blk_file, 2); if that fails, ksceVopCleanup(blk_vp, blk_file, 0, 0) (0x80010030 = not implemented ignored); unlock

name: fat_free_set
notes: free count d+0x20 = n, valid

name: free_count_dec
notes: exFAT free_clusters--; FAT free count--; advances lowest-free hint past clus

name: free_count_inc
notes: inverse; lowers hint

name: cluster_to_sector
notes: clus >= 2: (clus-2)*spc + data_start + rootdir_secs; clus 0/1: FAT32/exFAT -> (root_cluster-2+clus)*spc + data_start, FAT12/16 -> clus*spc + data_start (the fixed root area starts at data_start). FAT reads spc from the BPB copy (secbuf+0xD)

name: time_now
notes: via relocated pointer @0x8101d008 = ksceRtcGetCurrentClock(&dt, 0) (UTC); fallback 2000-01-01 00:00:00; stores y,m,d,h,m,s

name: fat_attr_decode
notes: fi->attr (+0x39) = ent[0xB]; mode = attr_to_mode(mnt, attr) | 0x40 if ARCHIVE clear | 0x200 if attr&0x80; type (+2) = 6 for directories else 0. Unless the boot sector's BS_FilSysType (secbuf+0x36, the FAT12/16 position) starts with "UVFAT" (strncmp 5), everything is recomputed without the 0x200 bit and +4/+6 cleared, so only UVFAT-formatted volumes keep it. Returns 0

name: finfo_set_attr
notes: same mapping from an attribute value

name: exfat_attr_decode
notes: exFAT FileAttributes (+4) -> finfo

name: fat_attr_encode
notes: ent[0xB] = fi->attr

name: fat_datetime_decode
proto: void fat_datetime_decode(u16 *dt, u32 date, u32 time)
notes: y=1980+date>>9, m, d, h=time>>11, min, s=2*(time&0x1f)

name: exfat_tz_minutes
notes: UtcOffset byte: bit7 valid, 7-bit signed count of 15 minutes; invalid -> 0

name: dt_add_minutes
notes: adds minutes (the decompile was checked against the disassembly): minutes mod 60 with hour carry/borrow, then hours with at most one day of carry; when the day changed: past the month length -> next month day 1, day 0 -> previous month's last day (month 0 -> December's 31); month 13 -> next year Jan, month 0 -> previous year Dec. Month tables at 0x8101bc80 (leap: 31,29,...) and 0x8101bc98 (31,28,...), Gregorian leap rule

name: exfat_decode_times
notes: Create (+8, 10 ms +0x14, tz +0x16) -> fi+0x10 ctime, LastModified (+0xC, +0x15, +0x17) -> fi+0x28 mtime, LastAccessed (+0x10, tz +0x18, no 10 ms) -> fi+0x1c atime; seconds = 2*DoubleSeconds + 10ms/100; with the tz valid bit each is shifted by -offset*15 minutes (7-bit signed) via dt_add_minutes, giving UTC

name: cluster_read_block
proto: int cluster_read_block(u32 clus, u32 blk, uvfat_drive *d, void *buf)
notes: sector = cluster_to_sector(clus) + blk * (io_size >> bps_shift); blk_read(d, sector, io_size, buf)

name: blk_write
proto: int blk_write(uvfat_drive *d, ?, u64 sector, u32 len, const void *buf)
notes: write twin of blk_read: same checks, locking, pwrite (+0x4c, ksceVopPwrite) or lseek + write (+0x14, ksceVopWrite), sync/cleanup + one retry; 0x8032001A passes through, otherwise -12 (not -13). The dropped block is the same 64-bit shift case

name: fat_cache_flush
notes: only when fat_dirty (d+0xa0); clears it at the end. Windows are {first, count, buf, raw, start_sector, dirty, next}. FAT16/FAT32/exFAT: every dirty window in the LRU list is written, count*entry size rounded up to whole sectors, or fatcache_sz exactly. The target is start_sector plus, for FAT16/32, each copy k < NumFATs at k*FATSz (FATSz16 / FATSz32; mirroring is not controlled by BPB_ExtFlags). exFAT writes only the active FAT: VolumeFlags (+0x6A) bit 0 times FatLength (+0x54). Then the window's dirty flag is cleared. FAT12: allocates FATSz16*bps + 0x200 (512-aligned, NULL -> -15) and zeroes it. Windows tagged 0..3 (field +0x10 is the window index for FAT12) are repacked in order from u16 entries into 12-bit pairs; an odd last entry writes its low byte and nibble; the search stops at the first missing index, and the rest of the image stays zero. The whole FAT image is then written at BPB_RsvdSecCnt + k*FATSz16 for each copy. A blk_write error is returned at once and the FAT stays dirty. The NEON-heavy decompile was checked against the disassembly

name: fat_cache_load
notes: makes the FAT window holding clus the LRU head (clus >= nclusters+2 -> -0x20). FAT base sector: exFAT FatOffset (+0x50), plus FatLength when VolumeFlags.ActiveFat is set; FAT12/16/32 BPB_RsvdSecCnt, so FAT copy 0 is always read. Hit: move to front. FAT12: only when the whole FAT fits in four windows ((n+2)*2 <= 4*fatcache_sz, else -15). On the first miss the packed FAT (ceil(1.5*(n+2)) rounded up to fatcache_sz) is read with one blk_read, unpacked into windows 0..3 of fatcache_sz/2 u16 entries (field +0x10 = window index) and appended to the LRU tail; an already-used slot -> -15. FAT16/32/exFAT: per = fatcache_sz / entry size (4 for FAT32 and exFAT); first = clus rounded down to per; sector = base + (clus/per) * (fatcache_sz >> bps_shift); count = per, or (n+2) mod per for the short last window, which still reads a full fatcache_sz. A free slot of the 4 (buf == NULL) is used, else the LRU tail is evicted: if the FAT is dirty, fat_cache_flush writes every dirty window first; then it is unlinked and its buffer zeroed. The raw buffer (fatcache_sz+0x200, 512-aligned) is allocated on demand (-15). blk_read, and on success the window is pushed to the front. If the read fails, a fresh slot keeps buf set but is unlinked, so it is lost until unmount. NEON decompile, logic cross-checked

name: drive_flush
notes: exFAT: exfat_bitmap_flush first; PercentInUse (boot +0x70) is forced to 0xFF (not available) and the boot sector marked dirty if it was not already 0xFF. A dirty boot sector (d->boot_dirty) is written to sector 0 only; the backup boot region is untouched, which is fine as PercentInUse is outside the boot checksum. Then fat_cache_flush; fat_dirty cleared on success

name: uvfat_drive_unmount
notes: (g, d, opts): only for a drive with a device. Notes whether any open fd (mode != 0) or any of the 15 pins references d; this does not refuse the unmount. If mounted (state > 0): opts&0xFF == 2 (rw) -> drive_flush (an error is returned); the drive iterator buffer is freed only when nothing references d. Always frees the exFAT bitmap buffer, the upcase table (exfat_free_upcase) and every FAT window still linked in the LRU (raw buffer freed, descriptor zeroed); a window unlinked by a failed load leaks. Does not clear the drive slot itself; returns 0

name: cluster_write_block
proto: int cluster_write_block(u32 clus, u32 blk, uvfat_drive *d, const void *buf)
notes: sector = cluster_to_sector(clus) + blk * (io_size >> bps_shift); blk_write(d, sector, io_size, buf)

name: fd_flush_block
notes: no-op unless fd->flags (dirty). Block address: buf_clus 0 (fixed FAT12/16 root) -> buf_block counted from data_start; otherwise cluster_to_sector(buf_clus) + (buf_block mod blocks per cluster) * (io_size >> bps_shift). blk_write io_size bytes. Success: flags = 0 and fnode_touch(fd->fnode), so the owning fnode's mtime is stamped and dirty |= 4 on every block flush. Failure: flags |= 2, the error is kept for later

name: fat_count_free
notes: cached count if fat_free_valid; else loads every window (fat_cache_load) and counts 0 entries from cluster 2 to nclusters+1 (u16 for FAT12/16, u32 raw for FAT32/exFAT - the FAT32 top nibble is not masked); the first free cluster becomes free_hint; the result is cached (fat_free, valid = 1). Load error returned; window missing after load -> -15

name: fat_access
proto: int fat_access(uvfat_drive *d, int set, u32 clus, u32 *val)
notes: (d, set, clus, *val): free_hint is first raised to at least root_cluster; fat_cache_load + window lookup (-15 if absent). Get: u32 entry for 32-bit FATs (FAT32 top nibble not masked) or u16 (FAT12 is held unpacked), a free entry below the hint lowers it, the hint cluster in use advances it. Set: stores the value; if it changed, FAT12/16/32 adjust fat_free (when valid) for free<->used transitions and the hint (exFAT leaves counting to the bitmap), then the window and the FAT are marked dirty; an unchanged value dirties nothing

name: fat_set_eoc
notes: fat_access(set) with EOC 0xFFFFFFFF (exFAT), 0x0FFFFFFF (FAT32) or 0xFFFF (FAT12/16; FAT12 packs it as 0xFFF); the result is returned in r0 although the decompile shows void

name: fat_find_free
notes: scans window by window (fat_cache_load) from max(start, free_hint) for a 0 entry (u32 or u16); reaching nclusters+2 wraps once to free_hint and the scan stops at start, so after the wrap only [free_hint, start) is covered. While the hint's window holds no free entry past the hint, free_hint moves to the window end; a found cluster below the hint lowers it; values >= fat_eoc are skipped. None (or a load error) -> free_hint = nclusters+2 and 0x0FFFFFFF is returned for every FAT width; callers compare against fat_eoc

name: fat_set_run
proto: int fat_set_run(uvfat_drive *d, int op, u32 first, u32 last)
notes: exFAT only (else -15), window by window through fat_cache_load: op 1 writes FAT[i] = i+1 for first <= i < last (the entry for last is left to the caller, fd_extend links or terminates it); op 2 zeroes FAT[first..last); other ops or a missing window -> -15. Marks each touched window and the FAT dirty; the NEON/unrolled stores were checked to be plain fills

name: fnode_child
proto: int fnode_child(uvfat_fnode *parent, const char *name, u32 len, uvfat_fnode **out)
notes: parent must be a directory whose own parent is still valid (parent_cluster != -2) or the root, else 0x80010014 (ENOTDIR); parent name NULL -> ENOENT; path = parent path + '/' + name -> path_parse -> fnode_get (ENOMEM); the child inherits the parent's finfo, then its parent context is set to the parent's first cluster/flags/size; dir_lookup_name; failure releases the child (errno mapped); out NULL = existence check only (released); when the child has no other users (ref - nopen == 1) its chain is set up (fnode_set_chain)

name: fnode_getstat
notes: memset 0x58; finfo_to_iostat(drive->mnt, &f->finfo(+0x210), st); always 0

name: uvfat_dclose
notes: fdidx 0 or >= nfds -> 0x80010051; fd mode must be 3 (else 0x80010009 EBADF); directory whose parent is gone and is not the root -> ENOENT; non-directory -> 0x80010015; fd_release_idx

name: uvfat_close
notes: fdidx out of range -> 0x80010051; fd mode 1/2/6 else EBADF; only regular files (type 0, else 0x80010015); parent gone -> ENOENT; writable (2/6): fd_flush_block (failure: drive_flush and return the error), fnode_writeback, clear dirty, drive_flush; fd_release_idx

name: fnode_size
notes: f->size

name: uvfat_lseek
proto: int uvfat_lseek(u32 fdidx, ?, u64 off, int whence, u64 *out)
notes: fd mode 1/2/6, regular file, parent valid; whence 0 SET, 1 CUR (fd->pos), 2 END (size), other EINVAL; FAT drives refuse positions >= 4 GiB (0x8001001B EFBIG); stores and returns the new position

name: uvfat_read
proto: int uvfat_read(u32 fdidx, void *buf, u32 len, ?, u64 pos, u32 *nread)
notes: pread semantics: fd mode 1/6, regular file, parent valid; pos >= size -> 0 bytes; temporarily sets fd->pos = pos, fd_read_locked, restores fd->pos; *nread = bytes

name: uvfat_write
proto: int uvfat_write(u32 fdidx, const void *buf, u32 len, ?, u64 pos, u32 *nwritten)
notes: pwrite semantics: fd mode 2/6, regular file, parent valid; FAT: end >= 4 GiB -> EFBIG; end beyond volume size -> ENOSPC (0x8001001C); clusters needed = ceil(end/clus) - ceil(size/clus) + reserved quota: exFAT compares with the bitmap free count, FAT with the free count or by probing the FAT for that many free entries (fat_find_free), else ENOSPC; temporarily sets fd->pos = pos, fd_write_at, restores fd->pos

name: uvfat_fd_open
notes: fd_reserve(g, mode); validates type (1/6 regular file, 3 directory, 8 directory); increments ref and nopen (other fds open -> fnode_flush_fds); fd->fnode = f; fd_alloc_buf (failure releases); *err_or_idx = fd index or SCE error; returns the fd

name: uvfat_dopen
notes: directory only (else 0x80010015), parent valid or root (else ENOENT), orphaned/no name -> ENOENT; a directory recorded as its own parent -> 0x8001002F; fd mode 3 via fd_reserve (none -> EMFILE), ref++/nopen++ (others open -> fnode_flush_fds), fd_alloc_buf, fd_rewind (position 0)

name: uvfat_open
notes: regular file only (type 0; directory -> 0x80010015), parent valid (else ENOENT), orphaned/no name -> ENOENT; internal fd mode = 6 (read/write) whenever flags&3 is 1, 2 or 3, else 1 - access mode is not enforced here and O_TRUNC is not handled; fd_reserve (none -> 0x80010018 EMFILE), ref++/nopen++ (others open -> fnode_flush_fds), fd_alloc_buf, fd_rewind; spins forever if the fnode has no drive (assert)

name: uvfat_dread
notes: fd mode 3 directory with valid parent (else ENOENT); drive iterator busy -> 0x80010078; copies the fd's position, cluster, extent cache and buffered block into the drive's embedded iterator fd (drive+0x118, mode 3), reads the next entry (exFAT: exfat_dir_find(1) into a temporary heap fnode; FAT: fat_dir_next_lfn giving LFN + 8.3), copies the iterator state back, releases the iterator; end -> ENOENT; d_stat via finfo_to_iostat, then acl_check_read(attr): EINVAL -> 0x8001000D and the dirent is zeroed; d_name = LFN (or the OEM 8.3 name converted) as UTF-8; >= 256 bytes falls back to the 8.3 name, or 0x80010034 if there is none

name: uvfat_chstat
notes: regular file or directory with a valid parent (else ENOENT / 0x80010015); orphan -> ENOENT; SIZE (bit 4) on a directory -> 0x80010015; working copy of the finfo; acl_check_read(attr) first; MODE (bit 1): acl_attr_from_mode(st_mode) supplies the low 3 attribute bits (with bit 0x10000 st_attr must equal the result, else EINVAL); bit 0x10000 (st_attr): new attr may not contain 0x08/0x40/0x80, may not toggle DIRECTORY, and must pass acl_attr_to_mode, else EINVAL; CT (8) <- st_ctime, AT (0x10) <- st_atime, MT (0x20) <- st_mtime; SIZE: FAT >= 4 GiB -> EFBIG, beyond the volume or not enough free clusters for growth (plus quota) -> ENOSPC; then fnode_set_info(f, finfo, set_mtime = bits&0x20)

name: drive_check_writable
notes: no drive -> ENOENT; read-only drive (opts low byte 1) -> 0x8001001E (EROFS); else 0

name: drive_set_trash
notes: drive+0x114 = f (pinned SceIoTrash directory fnode)

name: drive_drop_trash
notes: releases the pinned trash fnode (restored if release fails)

name: fnode_get_trash
notes: f->drive->trash

name: mnt_get_trash
notes: drive(m)->trash

name: fnode_mark_deleted
notes: dirty |= 1

name: fnode_free_clusters
notes: for a cluster inside the volume: NoFatChain exFAT files free their span from the bitmap (contig_free), others walk and free the FAT chain (chain_free); size := 0; first cluster := -1 for directories / 0 for files; clears NoFatChain; always resets the extent cache

name: uvfat_remove
notes: orphan in the trash (dirty&1): its directory is the drive's pinned trash; else dir required (NULL -> EINVAL); dir must be a directory with a valid parent (else 0x80010014); different drive -> 0x80010012 (EXDEV); names missing -> ENOENT; f a directory -> 0x80010015; drive iterator busy -> 0x80010078; dir_delete_entry(last component); on success: a referenced fnode is orphaned (parent -2, path cleared) and its clusters are freed now if no fd is open (else at the last close, fd_release)

name: uvfat_rmdir
notes: same checks as uvfat_remove but f must be a directory; emptiness: opens the directory on the drive iterator and reads one entry (exFAT exfat_dir_find(1), FAT fat_dir_next_sfn which skips . and ..); any entry -> 0x8001005A (ENOTEMPTY); then dir_delete_entry, orphaning and cluster freeing as for remove

name: uvfat_mkdir
proto: int uvfat_mkdir(uvfat_fnode *dir, const char *name, u32 len, int mode, uvfat_fnode **out)
notes: dir must be a valid directory (else ENOENT / 0x80010015); orphan -> ENOENT; path = dir + name -> path_parse -> fnode_get (ENOMEM); read-only drive -> EROFS; mkdir_core; drive_flush (also on failure); fnode_set_chain; the fnode's path is upcased (cache key); *out = new fnode, released on failure

name: uvfat_create
proto: int uvfat_create(uvfat_fnode *dir, const char *name, u32 len, int mode, uvfat_fnode **out)
notes: dir must be a valid directory; orphan -> ENOENT; read-only drive -> EROFS (0x8001001E); path_join_parse; create_core; first reference: extent cache + empty chain; the fnode's path is upcased; *out = new fnode

name: uvfat_link
notes: both fnodes must be regular files or directories with a valid parent (else ENOENT / 0x80010015-ish via -6); ref++ on each (once if a == b)

name: uvfat_unlink
notes: both fnodes must be valid files/directories (else ENOENT / -6); each: ref == 1 -> fnode_release, else ref--

name: uvfat_rename
proto: int uvfat_rename(uvfat_fnode *src, uvfat_fnode *newdir, const char *name, u32 len, uvfat_fnode **out)
notes: newdir must be a valid directory (else ENOENT / 0x80010015); src orphan/no name -> ENOENT; drive iterator busy -> 0x80010078; t = fnode_get(newdir path + name) (ENOMEM); src->ref++ while working; t gets a copy of src's finfo (+0x210..+0x24f); dir_delete_entry(src's old name) FIRST, then t's parent context := newdir and dir_create_entry(new name) - not atomic: a failure after the delete leaves the file without a directory entry (the target-exists check is the caller's, rename_helper); src takes over t's path and parent context (src keeps its identity, so open fds follow), t is orphaned and released; drive_flush; src path upcased; fnode_rename_prefix moves cached descendants; *out = src

name: root_getstat
notes: attr from acl_root_attr (0xF: acl_attr_to_mode + acl_attr_from_mode(mode & 0x1B6)) | DIRECTORY, epoch times

name: uvfat_fsync
proto: int uvfat_fsync(uvfat_fnode *f, u32 fdidx, int no_devsync)
notes: f NULL -> EINVAL; read-only drive: no-op; fdidx 0: write back the dirty blocks of every fd on f (fnode_flush_fds), else fd index check (0x80010051) and that fd's block if writable; fnode_writeback; clear dirty; unless no_devsync: drive_flush + ksceVopSync(blk_vp, blk_file, 0) under the device vnode lock; on an invalidated mount (flags&0x4000) errors are reported as success

name: uvfat_cleanup
notes: like uvfat_fsync, but a failed block flush discards the fd's buffer (flags=0, fd_buf_invalidate) instead of failing; writeback and drive_flush errors ignored; blk_flush; always 0 (EINVAL for NULL, 0x80010051 bad fd)

name: uvfat_vfs_sync
notes: m NULL -> 0x80010013; read/write drive: uvfat_fsync(f, fdidx, no_devsync=1) for every writable fd on the drive; then drive_flush and blk_flush(m) (errors suppressed on invalidated mounts)

name: uvfat_vfs_umount
notes: no drive for m -> 0x80010013; flags 0: EBUSY (0x80010010) if any fd is open on the drive, else 0 (the actual teardown happens later in vop_inactive/close); flags 1 (force): m->flags |= 0x4000 (invalidated), uvfat_vfs_sync, release the pinned trash fnode, then under the fnode table lock free the block buffers of every open fd on the drive (modes 1/2/3/6; the fds stay allocated) and the extent caches of its fnodes, detaching referenced fnodes (drive = NULL); other flags EINVAL

name: drive_devinfo
notes: no drive -> ENOENT; devinfo_fill(drive, out, len, &g)

name: drive_max_filesize
notes: devctl 0x80000001: 8-byte value from the table @0x8101bb40 indexed by fstype-1 (FAT 0xFFFFFFFF, exFAT 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF); unknown fstype 0; no drive -> ENOENT

name: drive_set_quota
notes: no drive -> 0x80010013; drive_reserve(drive, bytes)

name: devinfo_fill
proto: int devinfo_fill(uvfat_drive *d, SceIoDevInfo *out, u32 len, uvfat_global *g)
notes: len 0x18 or 0x28 else EINVAL; +0x0 max = nclusters*clusbytes, +0x10 cluster size; free clusters from the exFAT bitmap count or the FAT count, minus reserved quota (floored at 0) -> +0x8 free bytes; 0x28 form: +0x14 = 0, +0x18 volume serial (exFAT @0x64, FAT32 @0x43, FAT16 @0x27), +0x1c 11-byte label (FAT32 @0x47, FAT16 @0x2B; exFAT: spaces), +0x27 = 0

name: drive_reserve
notes: bytes beyond the volume size or more than currently free -> ENOSPC (-10 mapped); else reserved_clusters = free clusters - bytes/clusbytes, so exactly `bytes` stay available to writers (writes and growth add reserved_clusters to their requirement)

name: drive_clear_quota
notes: no drive -> 0x80010013; reserved_clusters = 0

name: exfat_init_thread
notes: work-queue job "SceExfatInit": ksceIoMount 0x300 vs0, 0xB00 sa0, 0x400 vd0, 0x500 tm0, 0x700 ud0, 0xC00 pd0, 0x600 ur0; if not manufacturing mode: ux0 (0x800) when ksceSysrootIsNonRemovableCardMode, then ksceIoDevctl("sdstor0:", 5, "mcd-lp-act-entire", 0x12) and ("usd-lp-act-entire"), and ("gcd-lp-act-entire") (sdstor devctl 5 on the memory card, USB and game card devices; its meaning is in sdstor, not traced)

name: module_start
notes: exfat_vfs_register(0x8101d00c); exfat_shared_init (fail -> SCE_KERNEL_START_FAILED 2); ksceIoMount(0x200 os0); manufacturing mode: if SceSysrootForDriver_7B7F8171()==0 mount 0x800 ux0, 0x900 gro0, 0xA00 grw0, else 0x100 sd0 (retried with permission 1 = read-only on 0x8001000D) and 0x800; enqueue exfat_init_thread (work queue 0x10023)

name: path_elem_decode
proto: int path_elem_decode(exfat_mnt *m, const char *path, int *skip, u32 *len, char *buf, u32 buflen)
notes: path_parse(path) (errors returned); skip = offset of the first path element in path (leading '/' skipped by matching the canonical path), len = its byte length; mismatch with the canonical form -> EINVAL; with a buffer: the element is upcased with the drive's rules (name_upcase) and written as UTF-8 into buf (overflow -> 0 returned, no error; bad surrogate -> EINVAL); UTF-8 conversion failure of the canonical path -> 0x8001005B (ENAMETOOLONG) or EINVAL

name: vfs_init
notes: returns 0

name: vfs_fini
notes: returns 0

name: vop_ioctl
notes: returns 0x80010030 (unsupported)

name: trash_purge_one
notes: devctl 0x3803: no pinned trash -> ENOENT; uvfat_dopen(trash), uvfat_dread until an entry that is not open (entry_in_use 0); dread error (end -> ENOENT) closes and returns it; fnode_child for that name, uvfat_remove for regular files (S_IFREG) else uvfat_rmdir; fnode_put

name: vfs_get_root
notes: *vpp = the VFS info's cached root (vfs_data) if any; else: no exfat mount -> 0x80010013; root_getstat, vfs_root_fnode, vfsGetNewVnode(mnt, default vops), lock; dd=NULL, mnt, type 0x1002, state 1, size 0, fid 0, node_data = root fnode, acl_data[0] = root st_attr, ref_count 1; returned locked

name: vfs_set_root
notes: no exfat mount -> 0x80010013; acl_root_attr (ENOENT -> EINVAL) then root_open; regardless of errors fills the given vnode under its lock: dd 0, mnt, type 0x1002, state 1, acl_data[0] = attr, fid 0, size 0, node_data = root fnode (NULL on error)

name: vop_sync
notes: takes the mount lock (unmounted 0x80010013 tolerated); node NULL -> 0x80010013; uvfat_fsync(node, file ? file->fd : 0, a->flags as no_devsync)

name: vop_read
notes: nbyte 0 -> 0; mount lock (mount gone -> 0x80010013); when file->vp differs from vp file_same_entry is evaluated and discarded; uvfat_read(file->fd, buf, n, pos = file->position); position += n; returns n

name: vfs_sync
notes: takes the mount lock; if the lock call returns non-zero (already held) it passes NULL, so uvfat_vfs_sync returns 0x80010013; else uvfat_vfs_sync(mnt->data)

name: vop_cleanup
notes: mount lock (unmounted tolerated); node NULL -> 0x80010013; uvfat_cleanup(node, file ? file->fd : 0)

name: vop_link
notes: mount lock; uvfat_link(fvp->node, tvp->node)

name: vop_dopen
notes: mount lock; uvfat_dopen(node, &file->fd)

name: vop_open
notes: mount lock; uvfat_open(node, flags & ~SCE_O_CREAT, &file->fd); file_same_entry evaluated and discarded for stacked vnodes

name: vop_lseek
notes: mount lock; uvfat_lseek(file->fd, offset, whence) (CUR/END resolved inside); success sets file->position; returns the 64-bit position or error

name: vop_remove
notes: mount lock; dvp NULL is allowed (uvfat_remove(NULL, node) - the trash path for orphans); if the lock call reports it was already held the remove is skipped and that value returned; else uvfat_remove(dvp->node, vp->node)

name: vop_dread
notes: mount lock; loops uvfat_dread: retries 0x800F090D, skips 0x800F0916 results and ACL-denied entries (0x8001000D), skips entries named SCEDEL~... that are still open (entry_in_use), zeroing the dirent each time; end (0x80010002) -> 0, entry -> 1, other errors returned

name: rename_helper
notes: under the mount lock: renaming the pinned trash directory -> 0x80010010 (EBUSY); fnode_child(newdir, name) as an existence check: target exists -> 0x80010011 (EEXIST, existing files are never replaced); only ENOENT proceeds to uvfat_rename; other lookup errors returned

name: vop_rmdir
notes: mount lock; removing the pinned trash directory -> EBUSY; dvp NULL -> EINVAL; uvfat_rmdir(dvp->node, vp->node)

name: vfs_decode_path_elem
notes: mount lock (unmounted -> 0x80010013, decode_len 0); path_elem_decode(m, path, &skip, decode_len, buf, buflen); on success *path2 = path + skip, *path3 = *path2 + decode_len

name: vfs_umount
notes: mnt NULL -> EINVAL; no exfat mount -> 0x80010013; mount lock; uvfat_vfs_umount(m, flags); success clears the mounted bit unless the mount was invalidated (forced)

name: vfs_devctl
notes: no exfat mount -> 0x80010013; every command runs under the mount lock and needs a mounted volume. 0x3004 (privileged, in 0x18, u64 at +8): drive_set_quota. 0x80000001 (out 8): drive_max_filesize. 0x3001 (out 0x18/0x28, else EINVAL; needs SceSblACMgrForDriver_D7AD8471(pid, mnt_data->assign_name) == 1 else 0x80010030): drive_devinfo, and on ux0 (mnt_id 0x800) 32 MiB are hidden from the free size (0 if less). 0x3802 (privileged): drive must be writable; looks up SCEIOTRASH in the root, if absent acl_attr_from_mode(6) and uvfat_mkdir("SceIoTrash", mode 6) - an ENOSPC there becomes EIO unless the volume really has 0 free bytes; on success the fnode is pinned as the drive trash. 0x3803 (privileged): trash_purge_one. 0x3005 (privileged, no input): drive_clear_quota. Privileged = SceThreadmgrForDriver_332E127C() is 0x80 or 0x40, else 0x80010030; unknown commands 0x80010030

name: vop_fchstat
notes: -> chstat_common(vp, stat, bit)

name: vop_chstat
notes: -> chstat_common(vp, stat, bit)

name: vop_lookup
notes: mount lock; name not NUL-terminated: copied when name[len] == '/'; fnode_child(dvp->node, name, len) then fnode_getstat (failure puts the fnode back); vfsGetNewVnode(default vops), lock: type 2 if S_IFDIR else 1, state 1, mnt, dd = dvp, node_data = fnode, size = st_size, acl_data[0] = st_attr, fid from nop() (whatever r0:r1 held - effectively undefined), ref 1; returned locked; vnode failure puts the fnode back

name: vop_getstat
notes: memset 0x58; acl_check_read(vnode acl_data[0] attr) first; mount lock; fnode_getstat

name: vop_fgetstat
notes: same as vop_getstat for file->vp

name: mnt_ctx_free
notes: closes the block device file if open (vnode lock, ksceVopClose, vfsFreeFile, ref_count--), heap_fini(m) (non-zero argument: no-op), and when mnt_data is set finalises the mount fast mutex and frees the context

name: vop_unlink
notes: mount lock (unmounted tolerated); uvfat_unlink(fvp->node, tvp->node); on an invalidated (force-unmounted) mount whose drive is now idle (drive_busy_count 0): mnt->data = NULL, drive_unmount, mnt_ctx_free

name: vop_rename
notes: ndvp NULL = same directory as odvp; ndvp on another mount -> 0x80010001 (EPERM-valued, not EXDEV); rename_helper (EEXIST if the target exists, EBUSY for the trash); new vnode via vfsGetNewVnode, locked: dd = new parent, state 1, type/size/acl copied from ovp, node_data = the (renamed) source fnode, fid from nop() (leftover register value), ref 1 -> *nvpp; vnode allocation failure puts the fnode back

name: vop_write
notes: (Ghidra's decompilation is wrong here - it drops the loop; read from disassembly) nbyte 0 -> 0; mount lock (gone -> 0x80010013); loop: uvfat_write(file->fd, buf+done, n-done, pos = file->position + done) until n bytes, an error, or a 0-byte write; vp->size raised to fd_size if larger; file->position += done; returns done or the error

name: vop_pread
notes: nbyte 0 -> 0; mount lock; uvfat_read(file->fd, buf, n, offset) - a single call (no loop, unlike vop_write); returns bytes

name: vop_pwrite
notes: nbyte 0 -> 0; mount lock; one uvfat_write(file->fd, buf, n, offset) (no retry loop); vp->size raised to fd_size; returns bytes

name: vop_mkdir
notes: acl_attr_from_mode(mode) before anything (0x800F0916-class -> EINVAL); mount lock; the trash directory as parent -> 0x8001000D; fnode_child existence check: exists -> EEXIST; ENOENT -> uvfat_mkdir; new vnode (type 2, size 0, acl_data[0] = ACL attr, fid from nop()) returned locked; if the vnode cannot be allocated the new directory is removed again (uvfat_rmdir) and its fnode put back

name: vop_create
notes: same as vop_mkdir for files: acl_attr_from_mode(mode); trash parent -> EACCES; exists -> EEXIST; uvfat_create; new vnode type 1 size 0; vnode allocation failure removes the new file again (uvfat_remove)

name: vop_inactive
notes: mount lock (gone tolerated); root vnode (type 0x1002): drop the trash pin; fnode_put(node); if the exfat mount is gone, invalidated or no longer mounted: when the drive is idle -> mnt->data = NULL, drive_unmount, mnt_ctx_free; when busy but invalidated and this is the root -> the same teardown; node_data = NULL on success

name: vop_whiteout
notes: delete-while-open: target directory = the drive's pinned trash, or dvp's own directory when none is pinned; the ret_enoent() existence stub always lets it proceed; a placeholder vnode is allocated and freed again (unused); rename_helper(ovp, target dir, new_path = iofilemgr's SCEDEL~ name) - EEXIST if taken; when moved into the trash the fnode is marked deleted (dirty|=1, so the last close frees it); the resulting fnode reference is put back

name: vop_dclose
notes: mount lock; uvfat_dclose(file->fd); invalidated mount with an idle drive -> teardown (drive_unmount, mnt_ctx_free); file->fd = 0 on success

name: vop_close
notes: mount lock; uvfat_close(file->fd); invalidated mount with an idle drive -> teardown; file->fd = 0 on success

name: vfs_mount
notes: first mount of this SceVfsMount: allocates exfat_mnt (0x230, ENOMEM), mnt_data/blk_vp recorded, fast mutex "SceExfatfsDrive" + uppercased assign name (attr 0x2000); flags |= 0x2000 (mounting); locks the device vnode (mnt->mnt_vnode), vfsAllocateFile(name); open mode: read-only (file flags 1) when the mount has SCE_VFS_MOUNT_FLAG_RDONLY; otherwise, for device vnodes (type & 0x2000), ksceVfsOpDevctl(cmd 1, out 0x10): write-protect bit -> 0x8001001E, devctl unsupported -> RW; ksceVopOpen; device vnode ref_count++; drive_mount(vflags 0x80000001 if the file is read-only else 0x80000000); failure: flags |= 0x20, closes the device file and frees the context; success: mnt->data = m; invalidated meanwhile -> teardown and 0x80010013; else mounted bit; mnt->available_entry_num = 0x40; default_io_cache_size = min(cluster, 0x8000)

name: exfat_vfs_register
notes: vi->vfs_ops = 0x8101bbc8 and vi->default_vops = 0x8101bc08; ksceVfsAddVfs; 0x80010011 (already registered) treated as success

name: blk_read
proto: int blk_read(uvfat_drive *d, ?, u64 sector, u32 len, void *buf)
notes: len must be a multiple of 512 (else -0x20); needs the block device open (mnt blk_vp +0x224, blk_file +0x228, blk_fd +0x22c != -1) and vfsLockVnode(blk_vp). byte offset = sector << bps_shift (d+0xb8). The device vnode's ops (vp+0x40): pread (+0x48) -> ksceVopPread; else lseek (+0x18) + read (+0x10) -> ksceVopLseek then ksceVopRead (a mismatched seek result counts as 0x80010005); neither -> 0x80010030. On failure: ksceVopSync(vp, file, 2); if the sync fails, ksceVopCleanup(vp, file, 0, 0), and only a 0 or 0x80010030 result allows the single retry. Final result: 0x8032001A (media removed) passes through, short or failed transfers -> -13. The 'unreachable' blocks Ghidra dropped are the shift >= 32 halves of the 64-bit shift, which cannot occur (bps_shift 9..12)

name: (cp_oem_to_ucs2 cases 13/16)
notes: not a function: Ghidra split two case bodies of cp_oem_to_ucs2 off its switch (0x81000b0e: r8 = sjis_to_ucs2, 0x81000b18: r8 = big5_to_ucs2, both rejoin at 0x810009ae); read from the disassembly

name: uv_alloc
notes: <=0x800: pathbuf_alloc (cached 0x800 buffers) else exfat_malloc

name: uv_free
notes: pathbuf_free

name: exfat_name_hash
notes: exFAT NameHash: per byte (lo then hi) hash = ((hash&1)<<15 | hash>>1) + byte

name: u16_strncat
proto: void u16_strncat(u16 *d, const u16 *s, int n)

name: entry_in_use
notes: dir path + de->d_name (strnlen 0x100) -> path_join_parse -> upcased path; returns fnode_find (live fnode ref count, i.e. nonzero if open); *err = 0, ENOMEM, ENOENT (orphaned dir)

name: fd_read_locked
proto: int fd_read_locked(uvfat_global *g, u32 fdidx, void *buf, u32 len)
notes: fdidx < nfds (else -0x30), fd mode 1/6 (else -2); 0 for len 0, empty file or pos >= size; else drive_lock, fd_read(g, drive, fd, buf, len, 1), drive_unlock; returns bytes or error

name: fd_write_at
proto: int fd_write_at(uvfat_global *g, u32 fdidx, const void *buf, u32 len)
notes: fd mode 2/6 (else -2), fdidx < nfds (else -0x30); FAT: pos+len must stay below 4 GiB (else -0x20); pos beyond size: zero-fills from the size up to pos in io-size pieces (fd_write of a zeroed buffer); then fd_write(buf, len); drive opts 0x100 (write-through; only from mount flag bit 1, which vfs_mount never sets on 3.65): fd_flush_block + fd_close_touch after each write

name: fnode_find
notes: ref count of the fnode with this drive and path (ref>0, has a name), 0 if none

name: fnode_get_thunk
notes: tail call fnode_get

name: fnode_rename_prefix
proto: int fnode_rename_prefix(uvfat_global *g, uvfat_drive *d, const u16 *old, int ?, const u16 *new)
notes: after a directory rename: every live fnode on the drive whose path starts with old and continues with '/' or ends gets the prefix replaced by new (tail staged in the drive's root fnode path buffer as scratch), name pointer adjusted; result longer than 0x104 -> 0x8001005B (ENAMETOOLONG)

name: fnode_get_parent
notes: path longer than 0x104 -> NULL; copies the path, cuts at the last '/' ("/" for top-level entries), fnode_get

name: fnode_release
notes: _ReleaseFnode: takes the fnode table lock only for detached fnodes (drive NULL; attached ones rely on the drive lock); ref 1 -> wiped; ref--; -0xF if the lock fails

name: fnode_wipe
notes: reset to empty (same as the ref==1 path)

name: create_core
proto: int create_core(uvfat_global *g, uvfat_fnode *parent, name_info *ni, u32 mode, uvfat_fnode **out)
notes: parent must have a drive (-0x20); fnode_get(new path) (-0x16 if full); if that fnode already holds an entry (non-zero ctime year): -6 for a directory, -9 (EEXIST) for a file; parent context from parent; attr 0x20 (ARCHIVE) then acl_attr_from_mode(mode) and finfo_set_attr; ctime/mtime/atime := now (FAT: atime time-of-day zeroed); size 0, first cluster 0, sec_flags 1 (AllocationPossible); dir_create_entry; out NULL -> released; failure releases the fnode

name: fd_reset
notes: pos 0, clus -2 (0), clus_idx 0x0FFFFFFF

name: fd_alloc_buf
notes: io_size + 0x200 bytes (0x400 without a drive) via uv_alloc, 512-aligned into fd->buf, raw pointer in fd->buf_raw; ENOMEM 0x8001000C

name: fd_release
notes: frees the block buffer; fnode open count--; when that was the last open of an orphaned fnode (deleted while open) its clusters are freed now (fnode_free_clusters); fd->fnode = NULL; fnode reference released (wipe at ref 1; table lock only for detached fnodes); fd->mode = 0

name: fd_reserve
notes: _ReserveUnusedFd: first fd with mode 0 from index 1; none free: appends one more initialised slot while nfds < fd_cap (512, the pool is never reallocated, so at most 511 fds); the chosen fd gets the mode, position 0, cluster -2, no buffer; returns its index, or nfds (callers treat >= nfds as EMFILE)

name: fd_release_idx
notes: fd_release(&g->fds[fdidx])

name: check_parent_directory_data
notes: _check_parent_directory_data: only for paths below the root; gets the parent fnode; if nobody else holds it (ref 1, so its data may be stale) re-reads the parent's own entry (root: fnode_lookup_child(root); else via its parent: path_walk when that is fresh too, else fnode_lookup_child); then copies the parent's first cluster, flags and size into f's parent context; releases what it took

name: fnode_set_info
proto: int fnode_set_info(uvfat_fnode *f, finfo *fi, int set_mtime, uvfat_global *g)
notes: setattr core: check_parent_directory_data; size change: to 0 -> chain from the first cluster freed later, first cluster 0, NoFatChain cleared; shrink -> walks to the last kept cluster (FAT chain; a broken chain -> notify_broken_chain and -0xF; NoFatChain: contig_check) and remembers the rest; grow (FAT beyond 4 GiB -> -0x20) -> internal fd (uvfat_fd_open mode 8) at the old size and fd_write(NULL, n, flags 0x101) in <=1 GiB steps, which allocates clusters without writing data (the grown region keeps old disk contents), then fd_flush_block; mode/type/ctime/atime/attr (and mtime when set_mtime) copied when the finfo differs; fnode_writeback FIRST, then the cut-off tail is freed (NoFatChain: contig_free; else fat_set_eoc on the last kept cluster + chain_free), extent cache reset; drive_flush

name: mkdir_core
proto: int mkdir_core(uvfat_global *g, uvfat_fnode *parent, name_info *ni, u32 mode, uvfat_fnode *f)
notes: drive iterator busy -> -1; drive unmounted -> -5; cached entry exists -> -9 (EEXIST); attr DIRECTORY(0x10) through acl_attr_from_mode (failure -0xF); ctime/atime now (FAT: atime time-of-day zeroed), mtime via fnode_touch; one free cluster (cluster_find_free; none -> -10 ENOSPC); writes the first io block - FAT: '.' (own cluster) and '..' (parent cluster, 0 when the parent is the root; attribute = parent's, or computed via acl_attr_from_mode_level(0x80) when the parent attr is 0x0F) with times - then zero blocks for the rest of the cluster; size = one cluster; exFAT sec_flags 3 (NoFatChain), FAT: fat_set_eoc; dir_create_entry; on failure the cluster is released again (FAT entry 0 / bitmap bit cleared)

name: chstat_common
notes: validates CT (st+0x10), MT (st+0x30), AT (st+0x20) with datetime_valid; MODE: acl_attr_from_mode(st_mode) (failure 0x800F0916-class -> EINVAL); bit 0x10000: acl_inherit_attr(st_attr, acl result); mount lock; the pinned trash directory -> 0x8001000D (EACCES); uvfat_chstat; on success vp->size := st_size (SIZE) and vp acl_data[0] := ACL attr (MODE/0x10000); on failure with SIZE vp->size is re-read from the fnode

name: ucs2_to_dbcs936_949
proto: void ucs2_to_dbcs936_949(int cp, u8 lo, u8 hi, u8 *b0, u8 *b1)
notes: (reached via pointer from cp_ucs2_to_oem) cp 0xE GBK: U+20AC -> 0x80, U+0080 -> 0xA1F6; cp 0xF UHC (table @*0x8101d058, 0x7D rows); ASCII passthrough; linear table search (0xBF trails per row, lead 0x81+); unmappable -> 0xA1F6 (GBK) / 0xA1E1 (UHC)
